lessons.title: First Steps in BASIC
lessons.description: Print text, store numbers in variables, and do arithmetic.

checkpoints.title: Say hello
checkpoints.description: Use PRINT to display exactly: Hello, World!
checkpoints.starter_code:
10 REM Add a PRINT statement on line 20
30 END
checkpoints.solution:
10 REM Add a PRINT statement on line 20
20 PRINT "Hello, World!"
30 END
hints: Put the text inside double quotes: PRINT "Hello, World!"

checkpoints.title: Variables and arithmetic
checkpoints.description: W and H hold a rectangle's width and height. Store W * H in A and print A.
checkpoints.solution:
10 LET W = 6
20 LET H = 7
30 LET A = W * H
40 PRINT A
50 END
hints: Use LET A = W * H on line 30.

lessons.title: Loops and Decisions in BASIC
lessons.description: Repeat work with FOR/NEXT and choose with IF/THEN.

checkpoints.title: Count with FOR
checkpoints.description: Print the numbers 1 to 5, one per line, using a FOR loop.
checkpoints.starter_code:
10 FOR I = 1 TO 3
20 PRINT I
30 NEXT I
checkpoints.solution:
10 FOR I = 1 TO 5
20 PRINT I
30 NEXT I

checkpoints.title: Only the even numbers
checkpoints.description: Loop from 1 to 10 but print a number only when it is even.
checkpoints.starter_code:
10 FOR I = 1 TO 10
20 PRINT I
30 NEXT I
checkpoints.solution:
10 FOR I = 1 TO 10
20 IF I MOD 2 = 0 THEN PRINT I
30 NEXT I
hints: I MOD 2 is 0 for even numbers.
IF I MOD 2 = 0 THEN PRINT I

lessons.title: Talking with PILOT
lessons.description: Type text and compute values with PILOT's one-letter commands.

checkpoints.title: Type a line
checkpoints.description: Use the T: command to type exactly: Hello, World!
checkpoints.starter_code: R: T: types text on the screen
checkpoints.solution:
R: T: types text on the screen
T:Hello, World!
hints: Text after T: is printed as-is.

checkpoints.title: Compute and show a value
checkpoints.description: Use C: to set #X to 6 * 7, then type: The answer is 42
checkpoints.solution:
C:#X = 6 * 7
T:The answer is #X
hints: C: evaluates an expression and stores it.

lessons.title: Labels, Jumps and Subroutines in PILOT
lessons.description: Control program flow with J: (jump) and U: (use a subroutine).

checkpoints.title: Jump over a line
checkpoints.description: Make the program print Start then Finished, skipping the middle line with J:.
checkpoints.solution:
T:Start
J:*DONE
T:Skipped
*DONE
T:Finished

checkpoints.title: Call a subroutine
checkpoints.description: Use U:*GREET to run the subroutine, then print Back. Output: Main, Hello from GREET, Back.
checkpoints.starter_code:
T:Main
T:Back
E:
*GREET
T:Hello from GREET
E:
checkpoints.solution:
T:Main
U:*GREET
T:Back
E:
*GREET
T:Hello from GREET
E:
hints: U:*LABEL runs the code at *LABEL until E: and then returns.
Put U:*GREET between the two T: lines.

lessons.title: Turtle Shapes in Logo
lessons.description: Steer the turtle with FORWARD and RIGHT, and repeat moves with REPEAT.

checkpoints.title: Draw a square
checkpoints.description: Draw a closed square with 4 sides of 100 steps using REPEAT.
checkpoints.solution: REPEAT 4 [FORWARD 100 RIGHT 90]
hints: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right-angle turns.

checkpoints.title: Draw a triangle
checkpoints.description: Draw a closed equilateral triangle. The turtle must turn 120 degrees at each corner.
checkpoints.solution: REPEAT 3 [FORWARD 100 RIGHT 120]
hints: The outside turns of any closed shape add up to 360 degrees.

lessons.title: Logo Procedures
lessons.description: Teach the turtle new words with TO ... END and reuse them.

checkpoints.title: Define SQUARE
checkpoints.description: Finish the SQUARE procedure so SQUARE 50 draws a closed square of side :SIZE.
checkpoints.solution:
TO SQUARE :SIZE
  REPEAT 4 [FORWARD :SIZE RIGHT 90]
END
SQUARE 50
hints: Inside the procedure, :SIZE is the side length.

checkpoints.title: A ring of squares
checkpoints.description: Use your SQUARE procedure 4 times, turning 90 degrees between each, to draw 16 sides.
checkpoints.starter_code:
TO SQUARE :SIZE
  REPEAT 4 [FORWARD :SIZE RIGHT 90]
END
SQUARE 50
checkpoints.solution:
TO SQUARE :SIZE
  REPEAT 4 [FORWARD :SIZE RIGHT 90]
END
REPEAT 4 [SQUARE 50 RIGHT 90]
hints: Procedures can be called inside REPEAT.

lessons.title: Prolog Facts and Rules
lessons.description: State facts, ask queries, and derive new knowledge with rules.

checkpoints.title: Ask about a fact
checkpoints.description: Write a query that finds who tom is the parent of and writes the answer.
checkpoints.solution:
parent(tom, bob).
parent(bob, ann).
?- parent(tom, X), write(X), nl.

checkpoints.title: Write a rule
checkpoints.description: Define grandparent(X, Z) using parent twice so the query prints ann.
checkpoints.starter_code:
parent(tom, bob).
parent(bob, ann).
?- grandparent(tom, Z), write(Z), nl.
checkpoints.solution:
parent(tom, bob).
parent(bob, ann).
grandparent(X, Z) :- parent(X, Y), parent(Y, Z).
?- grandparent(tom, Z), write(Z), nl.
hints: grandparent(X, Z) :- parent(X, Y), parent(Y, Z).

lessons.title: Prolog Arithmetic and Recursion
lessons.description: Evaluate expressions with is/2 and define recursive predicates.

checkpoints.title: Evaluate with is
checkpoints.description: Compute 6 * 7 with is/2 and write the result.
checkpoints.solution: ?- X is 6 * 7, write(X), nl.
hints: = only unifies terms; is evaluates arithmetic.

checkpoints.title: Recursive factorial
checkpoints.description: Complete the recursive clause so factorial(5, F) gives 120.
checkpoints.solution:
factorial(0, 1).
factorial(N, F) :- N > 0, N1 is N - 1, factorial(N1, F1), F is N * F1.
?- factorial(5, F), write(F), nl.
hints: factorial(N, F) :- N > 0, N1 is N - 1, factorial(N1, F1), F is N * F1.
